scoring_inputs.source: CHIRPS (ClimateSERV) rain vs crop water demand

insights.title: Rain is more than crops can use
insights.body: Rain exceeds crop water demand by about 455 mm a year. Waterlogging and runoff are bigger risks than drought.

insights.title: Fields are greenest in September, barest in March
insights.body: Satellite greenness of the farmland here peaks at 0.68 and drops to 0.37 (0 = bare, 1 = dense crop). The low months are when soil is most exposed to rain and wind.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Maize, Chickpea and Potato score highest on climate, water and soil fit.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: In a dry year, rain can drop to about 1,446 mm
consequences.detail: That is 18% below the 1,753 mm average; about 1 year in 10 is this dry or worse.
consequences.action: Keep a drought-tolerant crop in the plan as insurance.

consequences.headline: No clear long-term change since 2001
consequences.detail: Rain, heat and dry spells show no reliable trend here. The bigger risk is the swing from one year to the next.
consequences.action: Plan for a bad year rather than a changing average.
